phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Evaluate the definite integral f(3) - f(1) = ∫₁³ √x/(1+x)² dx.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Substitute √x = tan θ (so x = tan²θ, dx = 2 tan θ sec²θ dθ). The denominator (1+x)² becomes (1+tan²θ)² = sec⁴θ. The integral simplifies nicely using basic trigonometric identities.

key_concepts: Limits change: x=1 → θ=π/4, x=3 → θ=π/3

key_formulas.substitution: √x = tan θ  ⇒  dx = 2 tan θ sec²θ dθ
key_formulas.integrand: (tan θ · 2 tan θ sec²θ dθ) / sec⁴θ = 2 tan²θ / sec²θ dθ = 2 sin²θ dθ

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Express f(3) - f(1) as a definite integral from 1 to 3, substitute √x = tan θ, change limits, convert to 1 - cos(2θ), integrate and evaluate.
logical_steps: Step 2: Put √x = tan θ, dx = 2 tan θ sec²θ dθ
Step 3: Change limits: x=1 → θ=π/4; x=3 → θ=π/3
Step 4: Simplify integrand to 2 sin²θ = 1 - cos(2θ)
Step 5: Integrate [θ - (1/2)sin(2θ)] from π/4 to π/3
Step 6: Evaluate numerical result and match option

step_4_simplify_integrand.I: ∫_{π/4}^{π/3} (tan θ · 2 tan θ sec²θ) / sec⁴θ dθ
